title: Injective module transport along representable stack morphisms
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Give each stack its big etale site: objects and arrows are those of its category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], coverings lie over jointly surjective etale scheme families, and $\mathcal O(x)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ on an object over $T$ [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Module sheaves mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and injective means [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Precomposition $a^*M(x)=M(a(x))$, with its unchanged section rings, is an exact functor and is left adjoint to the direct image $a_*$ given by $(a_*N)(y)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T})$ for $y$ over $T$. Thus $a_*$ preserves injectives. If $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces, meaning that every scheme base change is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], then $a^*$ also preserves injectives. No smoothness, flatness, quasi-coherence, separation, or quasi-compactness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 06X2 (lemma-pullback-injective-modules) together with Tag 06WX (lemma-pushforward-injective); exact module adjunction and precomposition in section-modules. The representable specialization uses Tag 04Y5 (algebraic.tex, lemma-characterize-representable-by-algebraic-spaces) and Tag 06WY (lemma-fibre-products).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] over the big etale scheme site. Both total categories are small in the universes of the statement and every arrow is cartesian, so $a$ is continuous and cocontinuous. As $a$ lies over schemes, $a(x)$ lies over exactly the same $T$ as $x$; consequently $\mathcal O_{\mathcal B}(a(x))=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=\mathcal O_{\mathcal A}(x)$, and restrictions on these rings coincide. Thus module precomposition has the original actions and restriction maps. By the exactness assertion of [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data], this functor is additive and exact on all module sheaves.

source.place: Tags 06TS, 06TW and 06WE, with the etale variant following section-modules

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] for $a$. Its inverse image is precomposition and its direct image is the compatible-family functor. At $y$ over $T$, the latter has entries $s_{x,\psi}\in N(x)$ for arrows $\psi:a(x)\to y$, compatible with all arrows between such pairs. The category of these pairs is equivalent to $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}(\mathit{Sch}/T)$: over $u:U\to T$, an arrow $a(x)\to y$ is uniquely the cartesian lift $u^*y\to y$ composed with a fibre isomorphism $a(x)\simeq u^*y$, by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. This correspondence and its inverse preserve arrows by that same unique-factorization property. Therefore compatible families are precisely global sections on this test fibre, giving the displayed formula for $a_*N$. Restriction along $y'\to y$ precomposes the indexing arrows, hence is the stated base-change restriction. The identical formula applies to rings and to their actions.

The ring equality in step 1 makes $\mathcal O_{\mathcal A}\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal B}}a^{-1}M$ canonically $a^{-1}M$, by $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$ and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with this identity structural map. Its module pushforward is the compatible-family functor of step 2 with the induced $\mathcal O_{\mathcal B}$-action. Thus precomposition is $a^*$ and $a^*\dashv a_*$. Since $a^*$ is exact by step 1, [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] shows that $a_*$ preserves injectives.

source.place: Tag 06WE and the tensor formula following it; Tag 06WX (lemma-pushforward-injective)

proof.text: Now assume $a$ representable by algebraic spaces. By [lem-sfb-faithful-stack-map-representable], $a$ is injective on all fibre Isom sets. It is faithful on the total categories as well: parallel arrows $b,c:x\to x'$ with $a(b)=a(c)$ have the same base arrow $u$. Factor both through a chosen cartesian lift $u^*x'\to x'$ by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Their fibre-isomorphism factors have equal images, since the image of the lift is cartesian; fibrewise injectivity makes the factors equal, hence $b=c$. By [lem-sfb-fibred-limit-calculus], $\mathcal A$ has fibre products and equalizers, and $a$ preserves both.

For each object $x$ over $U$, apply [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] to $\mathcal A/x$ and $\mathcal B/a(x)$. Both are equivalent as ringed sites to $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Under these equivalences the functor $a_x$ sends an arrow $z\to x$ to $a(z)\to a(x)$ and has exactly the same underlying scheme map. Hence its composite with the second equivalence is the first equivalence, so $a_x$ is an equivalence of sites. Its structural ring map at an object over $V$ is the identity of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. This verifies the local slice hypotheses, including their ring identifications.

source.place: Tag 06W9 (lemma-localizing-structure-sheaf), as used in the proof of Tag 06X2

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-slice-module-shriek-exact] with $u=a$, $R=\mathcal O_{\mathcal B}$ and $R'=\mathcal O_{\mathcal A}$. Continuity and cocontinuity are step 1, fibre products and equalizers with their preservation are step 4, and the equivalences on ringed slices are step 5. We obtain an exact additive functor $a_!$ with $a_!\dashv a^*$. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to this exact left adjoint: $a^*$ preserves injective module sheaves. Together with step 3 this proves both transport assertions. All uses concerned the ambient module categories on the big sites; no quasi-coherence or additional geometric hypothesis entered.
